honest_evidence: Threshold registry honest evidence: this record states which measured dimensions carry an agreed threshold and which carry an EXPLICIT absence. An absent dimension is never reported as satisfied and never defaulted to a value — it blocks promotion, because a default would silently manufacture a pass. The agreed values are bound to the measured reference they were agreed against (PRD §8).

sign_off.note: The signature covers ALL measured dimensions (M-1..M-5): M-1 on its 2026-11-23/24 basis, M-2..M-5 by the consolidated signature of 2026-11-24 (issue #2167). The promotion decision is therefore ALLOWED and the gate-compatible thresholds artifact derives against the measured reference.

value.scope: config A — the chunk/passage-level anchor metrics

M-1.surface: config A: the chunk-level anchor metrics (recall, precision, complete_recall, noise, retrieval_recall, passage_recall, recall@k, ndcg@k); config B: the doc-level source_documents — the surfaces differ by construction (pair E01), so the threshold applies per surface and never across them.
M-1.rationale: the operator signed these bounds on 2026-11-23 against the measured A-only reference (issue #2118 / MR !1056 — 6 evaluable cases: retrieval_recall 1.0, recall_at_10 1.0, ndcg_at_10 1.0, passage_recall 1.0, noise 0.667). Every bound is a line the reference satisfies and a later run must keep satisfying: a regression past it is visible instead of averaged away (PRD §8). The reference rests on a 3-chunk corpus (one document, the venue's upload-validation fixture) over 6 evaluable cases, where recall and ndcg sit at their ceiling — the bounds are a floor the later runs must keep, not a fine-grained regression detector on that corpus

value.scope: the content-blind attribution-trace surface over each leg's substantive answers (source identities only; the same shape on every leg, so comparisons stay valid)

M-2.surface: the content-blind attribution-trace surface over each leg's substantive answers (the judged pass's surface — source identities only; the same shape on every leg, so comparisons stay valid)
M-2.rationale: signed by the operator's consolidated signature of 2026-11-24 (issue #2167), derived from the judged pass over the FINAL A reference's capture (60 ok rows, judge ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b, temperature 0, instructions d629ff99e6273f3f): 0.733 ungrounded-or-partial measured on the 45 substantive answers. The bound is the measured line plus ~0.07 margin — the M-1 pattern (a line the reference satisfies that a later run must keep satisfying). The measured weakness of config A's attributed-grounding is recorded in the derivation method; the B-vs-C comparison carries the sharper signal. Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md

value.scope: the mechanical abstention-verdict rules over each leg's rows (config A: the answer-text prose signal, judged; config B: the mechanical abstained/abstention_reason fields)

M-3.surface: the mechanical abstention-verdict rules over each leg's rows (config A: the answer-text prose signal, judged; config B: the mechanical abstained/abstention_reason fields)
M-3.rationale: signed by the operator's consolidated signature of 2026-11-24 (issue #2167), derived from the judged pass over the FINAL A reference: 4/4 unanswerable cases abstained honestly (1.000) and 10/54 = 0.185 excessive abstentions on the answerable class — all ten restricted-visibility cases whose refusal is correct for config A's actual reach. The bounds are the measured lines plus margin; they tolerate that construction on the A reference while catching a later leg abstaining on ordinary answerable cases. Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md

value.scope: each leg's own recorded per-case wall_ms (config A: the capture-a protocol layer; config B: the in-container driver; config C: the row wall_ms) — never a cross-leg comparison

M-4.surface: each leg's own recorded per-case wall_ms (config A: the capture-a protocol layer; config B: the in-container driver; config C: the row wall_ms) — never a cross-leg comparison; the surfaces differ by execution conditions the report records as uncontrolled differences
M-4.rationale: signed by the operator's consolidated signature of 2026-11-24 (issue #2167), derived from the FINAL A reference's measured distribution (n=60: min 3620.5, median 5944.7, p90 8016.1, p95 8498.2, max 10512.5 ms) — the measured maximum plus ~43% headroom for shared-GPU jitter, cross-checked against the issue #2118 reference's own max (11443 ms over 9 cases; the two maxima sit in the same band). Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md

value.scope: the per-case served token consumption (prompt + completion, from the B/C rows' usage records) — the same quantity the deployment's AGENT_RUN_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS knob enforces fail-closed per run

M-5.surface: the per-case served token consumption (prompt + completion, from the B/C rows' usage records) — config A records no resource surface at all (the S4 checklist documents the absence), so the bound binds the legs that record one
M-5.rationale: signed by the operator's consolidated signature of 2026-11-24 (issue #2167): the bound number is the deployment's DECLARED ceiling (AGENT_RUN_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS=30000) — a fact of the deployment, not an invented default: the knob is REQUIRED and fail-closed (an unset knob answers 503 budget_configuration_missing, no run starts), it enforces exactly this quantity per run (the served prompt+completion total; reaching it is the honest typed budget_exhausted terminal), and the measured A reference carries no resource surface to derive from (the measured A max of 10512 wall-ms x3 headroom names the same order of magnitude). TO REVISIT after the first gated B measurement: the first B leg's usage records are the measured distribution this bound's next revision derives from. Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md
